## How is Your First Week Structured at a Language School Abroad?

Your first week at a language school, such as the College of English Language (CEL) in San Diego, California or Vancouver, British Columbia, typically starts with a Saturday arrival at your housing. Completing the online placement test and downloading the CEL App before flying are key preparatory steps. Monday mornings begin with an orientation and your first class, generally running from 8:45 AM to 12:00 PM. This structured approach helps international students settle in quickly, understand their daily timetable, and start their English language journey efficiently. CEL has operated for over 45 years, refining this process to ensure a smooth transition for all new students, whether they are pursuing general English or specialized programs like Cambridge exam preparation. Students are placed into classes ranging from A1 (beginner) to C2 (advanced) on the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR) scale. To ensure a strong start at your language school, complete the online placement test before you travel; this determines your class level and ensures you begin classes without delay. Also, download the CEL App for your schedule and housing details, which can be crucial for a smooth check-in. Plan to arrive on Saturday to allow time to adjust to any jet lag and explore your neighborhood before Monday's campus activities. This preparation minimizes stress and maximizes your focus on learning English. Getting comfortable with your surroundings a little ahead of time makes all the difference.

### What should students do before their first week at a language school abroad?

Before traveling to a new city like Vancouver or San Diego, students have three main tasks: completing the online placement test, downloading the CEL App, and uploading necessary documents. The placement test, sent via email, takes less than 30 minutes and determines your starting English level on the CEFR scale, ensuring you join the appropriate class without delay. The CEL App, available for both Apple and Android devices, provides your class schedule, housing details, student handbook, and the activity calendar. Many students find it invaluable for managing their first week. Finally, uploading your passport photo and other forms through the pre-arrival email saves time during Monday's orientation. These steps are designed to streamline your arrival and maximize your focus on learning English. For additional information on what to expect, students can also consult our general FAQ section about studying abroad.

### What happens on arrival weekend and your first Monday at a language school?

Arrival is typically on a Saturday, directly to your accommodation, not the school. Students have options for transport from the airport, including a pre-booked CEL airport transfer, ride-sharing services like Uber or Lyft, or public transport, which is particularly efficient in Vancouver via the Canada Line Skytrain. Arriving on Saturday provides a full day to unpack, recover from jet lag, and explore your neighborhood. On Sunday, students are advised to check the CEL App for their Monday class schedule and, if possible, walk the route to campus. Your first Monday at a CEL language school begins at 8:30 AM on campus. Classes run from 8:45 AM to 12:00 PM, followed by an orientation from 12:30 PM to 2:00 PM. This orientation covers essential information for your stay in the USA or Canada, including student services and local policies. From Tuesday to Friday, students follow a fixed daily timetable, primarily with morning classes, ensuring a consistent learning experience. Social activities organized by the school run throughout the week, helping students meet classmates and practice their English in a relaxed setting. To learn more about living arrangements, explore our housing options, including homestay programs.
